## Problem 6

# Data and Jags 6

```{r}
Y   <- gambia$pos
X   <- gambia[,4:8]
X   <- scale(X)

# Fit logistic model
mod <- textConnection("model{
obs_mean <- mean(Y)
#like
 for(i in 1:n){
  Y[i] ~ dbern(pi[i])
  logit(pi[i]) <- beta[1] + X[i,1]*beta[2] +
                  X[i,2]*beta[3] + X[i,3]*beta[4] +
                  X[i,4]*beta[5] + X[i,5]*beta[6]
 }
 for(j in 1:6){
  beta[j] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
 }
 
# Posterior preditive checks

  pred_mean <- mean(Y)
 D <- pred_mean 
 
}")

data  <- list(Y=Y,X=X,n=length(Y))
model <- jags.model(mod,data = data, n.chains=2,quiet=TRUE)
update(model, 5000, progress.bar="none")
samps <- coda.samples(model, variable.names=c("beta", "D"),
                      n.iter=20000, progress.bar="none")
```

```{r}
print(summary(samps))

```

# Checks for 6
```{r}

D0 <- mean(gambia$pos)
Dnames <- c("Mean")

pval1 <- rep(0,1)
names(pval1)<- Dnames
D1  <- samps[[1]]
pval1 <- mean(D1[,1]>D0)

```

# pval1
```{r}
pval1
```
Choose wrong value/method for examining D I guess. If not we should choose a different model as p-value is 0. I think the model should be good though as 
it uses some log reg (maybe use just that). 

## Problem 8

# Data for 8

```{r}
ovprop <- c(0.845,0.847,0.880,0.674,0.909, 0.898,0.770,0.801,0.802,0.875)
makes <- c(64,72,55,27,75,24,28,66,40,13)
totalattempts <- c(75,95,63,39,83,26,41,82,54,16)

x <- log(ovprop/ (1 - ovprop))
```

# Jags 8
```{r}
data   <- list(Y = makes, N = totalattempts , X = x)
params <- c("D","beta")

model_string <- textConnection("model{
   # Likelihood
    for(i in 1:10){
      Y[i]        ~ dbinom(p[i],N[i])
      logit(p[i]) <- beta[1] + beta[2]*X[i]
    }
   # Priors
    beta[1] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
    beta[2] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
    
  # Posterior preditive checks
  for(i in 1:10){
    Y2[i]    ~  dbinom(p[i],N[i])
    rate[i] <- Y2[i]/N[i]
  }
  D[1] <- min(Y2[])
  D[2] <- max(Y2[])
  D[3] <- max(Y2[])-min(Y2[])
  D[4] <- min(rate[])
  D[5] <- max(rate[])
  D[6] <- max(rate[])-min(rate[])
 }")
 
model <- jags.model(model_string,data = data, n.chains=2,quiet=TRUE)
update(model, 10000, progress.bar="none")
samples1 <- coda.samples(model, variable.names=params, thin=5, n.iter=20000, progress.bar="none")


```

```{r}
print(summary(samples1))
```

# Checks for 8

```{r}
rate <- makes / totalattempts
D0 <- c(min(makes), max(makes), max(makes)-min(makes),
            min(rate),max(rate),max(rate)-min(rate))
Dnames <- c("Min makes", "Max makes", "Range makes", "Min rate", "Max rate", "Range rate")

pval2 <- rep(0,6)
names(pval2)<-Dnames
D1  <- samples1[[1]]
  for(j in 1:6){
   pval2[j] <- mean(D1[,j]>D0[j]) 
  }
```

# pval2
```{r}
pval2

```
Model looks nice as the makes' and rates' p-values
are somewhat close to 0.5. The closest values to 1 and 0
are from max makes .81.
